newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac phones French right "dream team" before vote.
newsitem.headline: Chirac phones French right "dream team" before vote.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac telephoned socially-minded Gaullist Philippe Seguin and free marketeer Alain Madelin on Wednesday to boost the French right's last-ditch "dream team" before Sunday's election runoff, political sources said.
Seguin is a gruff National Assembly speaker tipped as a possible prime minister while Madelin is a former finance minister who could be reappointed if the centre-right wins runoffs on June 1.

Details of what they discussed were not immediately known. Talk of a Seguin-Madelin tandem is aimed at appealing to opposing tendencies in the fractious ruling coalition after Prime Minister Alain Juppe announced he would step down.

Seguin and Madelin appeared together at a rally in the southeastern city of Chambery on Wednesday as the centre-right desperately sought to head off the opposition left, which won most votes on the first round last Sunday.
Political commentators described the unlikely duo, who embody radically different approaches to economic and social policy, as "the marriage of the carp and the rabbit".
